Rashi on Yevamot 52a:11:1.hebrew: נתן לה כסף או שוה כסף - ואמר לה "התקדשי לי במאמר יבמין". ואע"ג דיהב לה מידי, לאו קידושין גמורים הן כקידושי תורה, שהרי אין קידושין תופסין באשת אח, והתורה לא התירתה לו ליעשות כאשה נכרית אלא כסדר המצוה, וביאה הוא דכתבה בה רחמנא:
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:11:1.english: He gave her money or the equivalent [value] of money - And he said to her, "Be betrothed to me with a levirate betrothal." And even though he gave her something, it is not a full betrothal like a Torah betrothal, for betrothal does not take effect with a brother's wife, and the Torah did not permit her to him to become like an unrelated woman, except according to the order of the mitzvah, and it is intercourse that the Merciful One wrote regarding her.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:11:2.hebrew: ובשטר כיצד - ואם קידש בשטר, כיצד כתב בו? והוינן "כיצד" בתמיה — והא כיון דקידושי כסף אמרת "נתן לה כסף" כשאר נשים, ממילא שמעינן שטר נמי כשאר כל שטר אירוסין בעלמא, כדאמר בקידושין: "כתב על הנייר או על החרס, אע"פ שאין בו שוה פרוטה, הרי את מקודשת" כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:11:2.english: And with a document, how - And if he betrothed [her] with a document, how does he write in it? And [the Gemara] asks, "How?" in astonishment — since [regarding] betrothal with money you said, "He gives her money," like other women, we automatically infer [that] a document too [is] like any other ordinary document of betrothal, as it says in Kiddushin: "[If] he wrote on paper or on earthenware, even though it is not worth a perutah, 'You are hereby betrothed [to me],'‍" etc.:

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:11:3.hebrew: אמר אביי - האי תנא לאו אשטר מאמר קאי, אלא אשטר כתובה קאי:
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:11:3.english: Abaye said - This Tanna is not referring to a document of ma'amar [levirate betrothal], rather he is referring to a document of a marriage contract.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:12:1.hebrew: על נכסי בעלה הראשון - ולא על של יבם. מאי טעמא? כדאמר בהחולץ (לעיל יבמות דף לט.), אשה הקנו לו מן השמים:
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:12:1.english: From the property of her first husband - And not from that of the yavam. What is the reason? As it says in [the chapter] HaCholetz (above, Yevamot 39a): They granted him a wife from Heaven.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:13:1.english: Gave her a bill of divorce - [A] yavam to his yevama.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:13:2.hebrew: מהו - לפוסלה על אחיו ועליו בהאי גיטא, דתיקום עליה בלא יבנה? האי גט לא מהני באשת איש להתירה לינשא, והכא נמי לאו גירושין למיקם בלא יבנה:
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:13:2.english: What is [the law] - [Is it effective] to disqualify her from his brothers and from himself with this bill of divorce, so that she is subject to [the prohibition of] "he shall not build"? This bill of divorce is not effective for a married woman to permit her to marry [another man], and here too it is not [considered] a divorce so as to be subject to "he shall not build."

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:13:3.english: To confuse [it] with a bill of divorce - and [come to] marry a yevama after a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:14:1.hebrew: הכא פסיל בכהונה - כהן שנתן גט כזה לאשתו, אסרה עליו, והלכך תיבעי לן אי מהני מדרבנן:
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:14:1.english: Here it disqualifies for the priesthood - A priest who gave such a bill of divorce to his wife renders her forbidden to him, and therefore it is a question for us whether it is effective by rabbinic law.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:15:1.english: Only from her husband - And he did not permit her to any man.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:16:1.hebrew: הרי זה גט - ואם נתנו משכנסה, הרי זו מגורשת, הואיל ובידו לגרשה משנכתב. ואי משום גט ישן, דקי"ל (גיטין דף עט:) בית הלל פוסלין, ותנן: איזהו גט ישן? כל שנתייחד עמה אחר כתיבה — הא איתמר בפרק הזורק (שם): אם נתגרשה, תנשא לכתחלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:16:1.english: It is a bill of divorce - And if he gave it to her after he married her, she is divorced, since it was in his power to divorce her from the time it was written. And if [you are concerned] because of an old bill of divorce — as we hold (Gittin 79b) [that] Beit Hillel invalidate [it], and we learned [in the Mishnah]: What is an old bill of divorce? Any [case] where he was secluded with her after [its] writing — behold, it was stated in the chapter [entitled] HaZorek (there): If she was divorced [with it], she may marry [another] ab initio.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:1:1.hebrew: האי גט אחר גט הוא - בתמיה, וכי זהו גט אחר גט דקתני רישא "וחכמים אומרים יש גט אחר כו'", ומפרש "כיצד עשה מאמר כו'"? דהיינו גט אחר מאמר:
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:1:1.english: Is this [a case of] a bill of divorce after a bill of divorce - [This is asked] in astonishment: is this indeed [the case of] "a bill of divorce after a bill of divorce" that the first clause [of the Mishnah] teaches — "And the Sages say: There is a bill of divorce after [a bill of divorce], etc." — and [then] explains, "How so? He performed ma'amar [levirate betrothal], etc."? For that is [a case of] a bill of divorce after ma'amar.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:1:2.hebrew: כדאמרן - בברייתא דלעיל, כיצד אר"ג כו', ובמתני' לא פירש:
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:1:2.english: As we said - In the baraita above, how Rabban Gamliel stated [the law], etc., and in the Mishnah it did not explain [them].

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:3:1.english: Since the Master said - In the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achim (above, Yevamot 29b).

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:5:1.hebrew: והתניא לוקה - ואין מלקות ארבעים אלא על דברי תורה, אלמא דאורייתא היא, והיכי אמרת קנה? וקמשני: האי לוקה לאו מלקות ארבעים הוא, אלא מכת מרדות — מכת רידוי — מדרבנן, שנהג קלות ראש בעצמו, ולעולם קנה:
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:5:1.english: But isn’t it taught [that he] is flogged - And forty lashes are only [administered] for [transgressing] words of the Torah; evidently it is biblical [law], so how can you say he has acquired [her]? And [the Gemara] answers: This [mention of] “is flogged” is not forty lashes; rather, [it is] lashes for rebelliousness — lashes of chastisement — by rabbinic decree, because he acted with levity toward himself, and in fact he has acquired [her].

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:6:1.english: As Rav would flog - [With] lashes for rebelliousness.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:6:2.english: Regarding one who betroths by intercourse - [He flogs him] because of promiscuity.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:6:3.hebrew: ואמאן דמקדש בשוקא - אפילו בכספא, דמנהג זילות ופריצות היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:6:3.english: And regarding one who betroths in the marketplace - [he would flog him] even [if he betroths] with money, for it is a practice of disrespect and licentiousness.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:6:4.hebrew: דמתפקר - לשון חוצפא, שמעיז פניו להתריס עם שליח ב"ד:
Rashi on Yevamot 52a:6:4.english: [One] who behaves irreverently - An expression of insolence, meaning he acts brazenly to contend with a messenger of the court.

Rashi on Yevamot 52a:9:1.english: His mother-in-law was suspected on account of him - His mother-in-law was suspected [of impropriety] with him.

Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:11:1.hebrew: על הנייר או על החרס - אר"ת: כר' אליעזר אתיא, דלרבי מאיר דאמר עדי חתימה כרתי לא מהני, דדבר שיכול להזדייף הוא; דבשטר קידושין נמי בעי ר' מאיר עדי חתימה, כדמוכח בפ"ב דקידושין (דף מח.), ובפ"ק דקידושין (דף ט. ד"ה כתב) פירשתי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:11:1.english: On paper or on earthenware - Rabbeinu Tam said: [This baraita] follows [the view of] Rabbi Eliezer, for according to Rabbi Meir, who says [that] the witnesses signed [on the document] effect [the legal act], it would not be valid, because it is something that can be forged; for regarding a document of betrothal as well, Rabbi Meir requires signed witnesses, as is evident in the second chapter of Kiddushin (48a), and in the first chapter of Kiddushin (9a, s.v. Katav) I have explained [this].

Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:11:2.hebrew: שאין בו שוה פרוטה - פירוש: ואינה מתקדשת משום כסף, אלא מקודשת מטעם שטר. גבי "שדי מכורה לך" בפרק קמא דקידושין (דף כו. ושם), שהמוכר נותן שטר — תימה: אמאי נקט "אע"פ שאין בו שוה פרוטה", דאין בו שום רבותא, דכך לי שוה פרוטה כמו אין שוה פרוטה? ויש לומר: דמשום דכתב ביה נתינה אחרי תיבת "את ספר המקנה", ס"ד דליבעי שוה פרוטה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:11:2.english: That it does not have the worth of a perutah - Explanation: She is not betrothed on account of money; [rather,] she is betrothed by virtue of a document. Regarding [the case of] "My field is sold to you" in the first chapter of Kiddushin (26a and there), where the seller gives a document — it is difficult [to understand]: why did [the Mishnah] state "even though it does not have the worth of a perutah," for there is no novelty in it, since [a document] worth a perutah is the same to me as [one] not worth a perutah? And one can answer: because "giving" is written in [the verse] after the phrase "the deed of purchase" (et sefer hamikneh), you might have thought that it requires the worth of a perutah.

Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:16:1.hebrew: לכשאכנסנה אגרשנה הרי זה גט - תימה, דבפרק כל הגט (גיטין דף כו:) אמרינן דאינו גט, שלא יאמרו גטה קודם לבנה. ובקונטרס פי' דהכא נמי לא קאמר דהוי גט אלא בדיעבד, שכבר נתגרשה בו. ואין נראה, דהתם דקאמר "אין גט" משמע דלא הוי גט כלל. ואר"ת דהכא כשכתב בו זמן שאחר נשואין, שהוא זמן נתינה, דאפילו גט ישן לא הוי, שלא נתייחד עמה אחר זמן הכתוב בגטה; והרי זה גט [דקאמר, היינו] לגרש בו לכתחלה. וההיא דכל הגט — שכתב זמן דקודם נישואין, וגרע טפי מגט ישן: דבגט ישן ליכא אלא ייחוד בעלמא, לכך אם נתגרשה בו תנשא לכתחלה; אבל התם דכנסה ואיכא ודאי ביאה — אינו גט כלל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:16:1.english: "When I marry her I will divorce her — this is a [valid] bill of divorce" - This is astonishing, for in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (Gittin 26b) we say that it is not a [valid] bill of divorce, lest people say her bill of divorce preceded her child. And Rashi explained that here too [the Gemara] only says it is a [valid] bill of divorce ex post facto, where she was already divorced with it. But this does not seem [correct], because there, when it says "there is no bill of divorce," it implies that it is not a [valid] bill of divorce at all. Rather, Rabbeinu Tam says that here [it refers to a case] where he wrote in it a date after the marriage, which is the time of delivery, so that it is not even an "old bill of divorce" [get yashan], since he was not secluded with her after the date written in her bill of divorce; and [what the Gemara says,] "this is a [valid] bill of divorce," means to divorce [her] with it ab initio. Whereas that [teaching] in Kol HaGet [refers to a case] where he wrote a date prior to the marriage, and it is worse than an "old bill of divorce": for with an "old bill of divorce" there is merely seclusion, therefore if she was divorced with it she may remarry ab initio; but there, where he married her and there were certainly marital relations, it is not a [valid] bill of divorce at all.

Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:4:1.hebrew: אם בעל ועשה מאמר פשיטא דהא קניה בביאה - הא לא פריך: "פשיטא דקניה בביאה לחודה", דמהא לא הוה משני מידי, אלא הכי פריך: פשיטא שמאמר אחר ביאה אינו מגרע, ואם בביאה לחוד קנה — בשביל מאמר שאחריו לא גרע. ומשני: "אימא אם בעל בלא מאמר קנה", דס"ד לא קני אלא אם כן עושה כמצותה — מקדש ואחר כך בועלה. וממתניתין דתנן בריש קידושין (דף ב.): "היבמה נקנית בביאה", לא שמעינן ליה, דדלמא היינו מדאורייתא. וכן הא דתנן הכא במתני' (לעיל יבמות נ:): "הבעילה בזמן שהיא בתחילה אין אחריה כלום", דלמא נמי היינו משום דמדאורייתא קני. ופריך: "והתניא לוקה"; וידע שפיר דמדרבנן לוקה, אלא דס"ד דלוקה מדרבנן משום דעשאוהו חכמים כפוגע באשת אח שלא במקום מצוה, וא"כ מדרבנן לא קני לה בלא מאמר. ומשני: מכת מרדות מדרבנן, ומשום פריצותא בעלמא, כדרב:
Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:4:1.english: If he engaged in intercourse and performed ma'amar [levirate betrothal], it is obvious, as he has acquired her by intercourse - [The Gemara] is not asking, "It is obvious that he acquires her by intercourse alone," because it would not be answering anything from that [question]; rather, this is what it is asking: It is obvious that ma'amar after intercourse does not detract, and if he acquires [her] by intercourse alone — because of ma'amar that follows it, it is no worse. And [the Gemara] answers: "Say: If he engaged in intercourse without ma'amar, he has acquired [her]," for it might have entered your mind [that] he does not acquire [her] unless he acts in accordance with its mitzva — [namely, that] he betroths [her] and afterward engages in intercourse with her. And from the Mishnah that we learned at the beginning of Kiddushin (2a): "A yevama is acquired by intercourse," we do not learn it, for perhaps that is [only] by Torah law. And similarly, that which we learned here in the Mishnah (above, Yevamot 50b): "Intercourse, when it is at the beginning, has nothing after it," perhaps that too is because by Torah law he acquires [her]. And [the Gemara] asks: "But wasn't it taught [in a baraita]: He receives lashes?" And [the questioner] knew full well that he receives lashes by rabbinic law, except that it entered his mind that he receives lashes by rabbinic law because the Sages treated him like one who encounters a brother's wife outside the context of a mitzva, and if so, by rabbinic law he does not acquire her without ma'amar. And [the Gemara] answers: [It refers to] lashes for rebelliousness by rabbinic law, and [it is] merely because of licentiousness, in accordance with Rav.

Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:6:1.hebrew: דמתפקר בשליח דבי דינא - כך גירס' הקונטרס, ויש ספרים שכתוב בהן "מאן דמצער שליחא דרבנן", וכן כתוב בכל הספרים בפ"ק דקידושין (דף יב:); ומיהו גם שם פי' בקונטרס: שליחא דרבנן — שליח ב"ד. ונראה דבכל שליחא דרבנן יש ללקות אע"ג דלא הוי שליח ב"ד, כדאשכחן בפ' עשרה יוחסין (קדושין ע.) דשמתיה רב יהודה לההוא טבחא דציער שלוחו; ואע"ג דשמתא חמור מנגדא כדמוכח במקום שנהגו (פסחים דף נב.), שמא החמיר עליו משום שביזה את רב יהודה עצמו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:6:1.english: [One] who acts insolently toward an agent of the court - This is the reading of Rashi, and there are texts in which it is written "one who distresses an agent of the Rabbis," and so it is written in all the texts in the first chapter of Kiddushin (12b); however, there too Rashi explained: "an agent of the Rabbis" — [meaning] an agent of the court. And it appears [to Tosafot] that for any agent of the Rabbis one is liable to be flogged, even though he is not an agent of the court, as we find in the chapter [entitled] Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 70a) that Rav Yehudah excommunicated a certain butcher who distressed his agent; and even though excommunication is more severe than flogging, as is evident in [the chapter entitled] Makom SheNahagu (Pesachim 52a), perhaps he was stringent with him because he disgraced Rav Yehudah himself.

Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:6:2.hebrew: דמקדש בביאה - אר"ת דאפי' ביבמה דצריך ביאה, דפריצותא הוא שעושה תחלת קנינו בביאה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:6:2.english: [One] who betroths by intercourse - Rabbeinu Tam says that even with a yevamah, where intercourse is required, [Rav flogs him,] for it is [an act of] immodesty that he makes the beginning of his acquisition through intercourse.

Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:6:3.hebrew: הדר בבית חמיו - אנן סמכינן אנהרדעי דאמרי: בכולהו לא מנגיד רב אלא אמאן דמקדש בביאה, דבשל סופרים הלך אחר המיקל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:6:3.english: One who dwells in his father-in-law's house - We rely on the Nehardeans, who say: Regarding all of them, Rav would not flog [anyone] except for one who betroths by intercourse, because in [matters of] rabbinic [law], follow the lenient [opinion].

Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:7:1.hebrew: דמבטל גיטא - אע"ג דרב משמע דסבירא ליה בריש השולח (גיטין דף לג:) דביטלו אינו מבוטל כר"ג גבי הא דאמר רב יוסף "ניחזי אנן", מ"מ קאמר הכא דלקי משום דמוציא לעז על הגט:
Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:7:1.english: [One] who nullifies a bill of divorce - Even though it is implied that Rav holds in the beginning of [the chapter] HaSholeach (Gittin 33b) that if he nullified it, it is not nullified, in accordance with Rabban Gamliel — regarding that which Rav Yosef said, "Let us see" — nevertheless, he says here that he is lashed because he casts aspersions on the bill of divorce.

Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:7:2.hebrew: דמסר מודעא אגיטא - אפילו היה מבטל כל מודעי, מ"מ היה מלקה אותו משום דמוציא לעז על הגט, דאיכא דשמע במודעא ולא שמע בביטול:
Tosafot on Yevamot 52a:7:2.english: Who delivers a declaration [invalidating] a bill of divorce - Even if he nullified all declarations, nevertheless [he] would lash him, because he casts a bad name upon the bill of divorce, since there are those who hear of the declaration and do not hear of the nullification.
